Abstract The adaptive immune system and neurodegenerative Alzheimer's disease (AD) are intertwined in multiple ways. Recent studies have reported alterations of the adaptive immune system in early AD stages, such as preclinical AD and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) due to AD. However, the identity of specific antigenic targets and whether the respective response is beneficial or detrimental during disease progression are still open questions. Herein, we describe cross-sectional analyses of blood and CSF from three different study populations covering early AD stages. We employed high-dimensional mass cytometry, single-cell RNA-sequencing, ex vivo T-cell secretome analysis, and antigen presentation assays to achieve a comprehensive characterization of adaptive immune cell populations. Our results show that subjects at the stage of asymptomatic, preclinical AD can mount a CD4 + T helper cell response towards amyloid-β peptide and display an early enrichment of CD8 + T effector memory cells re-expressing CD45RA (TEMRA cells) in CSF, combined with a less immunosuppressive gene signature of peripheral regulatory T cells. Conversely, in MCI we observed increased frequencies of CD8 + TEMRA/effector cells in the periphery characterized by a pro-inflammatory gene expression profile, and generally decreased antigen responsiveness. Our results demonstrate the complexity of adaptive immune changes in early AD and suggest that it may be beneficial to promote specific CD4 + T-cell responses in the preclinical stage, while in MCI it may be important to therapeutically target CD8 + T-cell responses if these prove to be harmful. Rickenbach et al. explore how the adaptive immune system changes in early Alzheimer's disease. They show that during the preclinical phase, a CD4+ T-cell response to amyloid-β epitopes emerges. In individuals with biomarker-positive mild cognitive impairment, however, there are signs of potentially harmful T-cell activity. See Skelly et al. Introduction Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disease affecting over 50 million people worldwide. 1 Hallmarks of AD pathology are aggregation and deposition of misfolded amyloid-β peptide (Aβ) into Aβ plaques, neurofibrillary tangles of hyperphosphorylated tau, and neurodegeneration. 2 After a long asymptomatic preclinical phase with Aβ accumulation followed by tau pathology, AD can progress along a continuum to mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and dementia. 3-7 Biomarkers for AD, including cerebral Aβ and tau aggregates measured by PET scans, along with elevated levels of phosphorylated tau species (p-tau) in CSF or plasma, can predict the probability of a clinical transition from cognitively healthy individuals to MCI and dementia. 8-10 Importantly, preclinical AD refers to cognitively normal individuals with increased risk, rather than a certainty of progression to MCI or AD, as many biomarker-positive, cognitively unimpaired individuals remain stable for extended periods while others do progress. 11 As particularly the preclinical phase of AD is not well understood, its in-depth characterization would allow improving biomarkers and potentially preventive therapeutic strategies before the onset of symptoms. In recent years, the role of adaptive immunity in AD has been increasingly recognized. Both clinical and genetic data suggest an involvement of inflammation-related pathways in AD pathogenesis and progression. 12 , 13 Multiple studies have identified increased T-cell infiltration in AD brains, 14-16 sparking the question of whether the underlying responses might be beneficial or detrimental during disease progression. For the CD8 + subtype of T cells, T effector memory cells re-expressing CD45RA (TEMRA) were shown to be increased in peripheral blood and CSF of AD patients. 14 Interestingly, immunophenotyping studies focusing on earlier stages of AD revealed that CD8 + TEMRA cells are altered even before the conversion to AD dementia 17 as early as in preclinical AD. 18 While lymphocyte infiltration in AD brains appears to be a targeted process, the antigenic target remains unknown. 19 Some studies investigated the T-cell antigen specificity in AD and reported reactivity of CD4 + T cells towards Aβ-derived epitopes in a human leucocyte antigen (HLA) class II-dependent manner. 20-22 These results were no surprise as earlier studies observed that immunization with Aβ peptide resulted in less AD pathology in mouse models of β-amyloidosis. 23 The subsequent first active immunization strategy for AD was AN-1792, mainly consisting of synthetic full-length Aβ 1-42 peptide. Clinical trials were suspended due to cases of meningoencephalitis. 24 Nevertheless, T-cell recruitment to the CNS occurred, and some responders mounted antibody responses against the amino-terminus (N-terminus) of Aβ. 25 Further discoveries of human autoantibodies directed against aggregated Aβ support the concept of successful priming of the adaptive immune system in AD. 26-28 To investigate the onset, targets and nature of AD-associated T-cell responses, we performed an in-depth cross-sectional immunophenotyping of three study populations covering the early stages of AD. We included cognitively healthy subjects with early evidence of cerebral β-amyloidosis (referred to as preclinical AD) and subjects with MCI due to AD (also referred to as prodromal AD). We provide a detailed analysis of immune cell populations in peripheral blood and CSF by combining mass cytometry by time-of-flight (CyTOF) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq). Additionally, we performed a functional analysis of the T-cell secretome and antigen presentation assays. We report that CD4 + T cells in preclinical AD display a type 2 T-helper profile and reactivity against carboxyl-terminal (C-terminal) and mid-sequence peptides derived from linear Aβ 1-42 . In contrast, we observe an increased frequency and a more pro-inflammatory gene expression of CD8 + TEMRA/effector cells in MCI subjects. Our analysis suggests a potentially beneficial role for activated CD4 + T helper cells in preclinical AD and a potentially harmful involvement of CD8 + T cells when the pathology becomes clinically symptomatic.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated altered T-cell reactivity and functional changes in adaptive immune cells across early Alzheimer's Disease (AD) stages, including preclinical AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). Using high-dimensional mass cytometry, scRNA-seq, T-cell secretome analysis, and antigen presentation assays, alongside multimodal imaging and fluid biomarker analysis (including AD-related biomarkers and anti-viral antibody titres), the research characterized immunophenotypes and function of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in blood and CSF. Key findings include: preclinical AD subjects showed an emergence of CD4+ T helper cell responses to amyloid-β peptide, early CSF enrichment of CD8+ TEMRA cells, and a less immunosuppressive peripheral regulatory T cell gene signature. Conversely, MCI subjects exhibited increased frequencies of peripheral CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells with a pro-inflammatory gene profile and generally decreased antigen responsiveness. The study highlights the complexity of adaptive immune changes, suggesting potentially beneficial roles for specific CD4+ T-cell responses in preclinical AD and harmful involvement of CD8+ T-cells in MCI, also considering immune tolerance and epitope mismatch in AD pathology.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational, Cross-sectional, and Diagnostic Study (Immunological Profiling)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, cross-sectional, and diagnostic study focused on immunological profiling and disease progression in early Alzheimer's Disease (AD) stages, specifically preclinical AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). No therapeutic interventions were applied. The study involved comprehensive analyses of blood and CSF from three distinct study populations (n=9, n=30, n=44), categorized based on CSF Aβ42/40 ratios (brain Aβ-negative/positive), Aβ PET imaging (FMM Centiloid >12 for Aβ positivity), and plasma p-tau217 levels (p-tau217+ and p-tau217-). Methodologies included high-dimensional mass cytometry, single-cell RNA-sequencing, ex vivo T-cell secretome analysis, and antigen presentation assays. Additionally, multimodal imaging, fluid biomarker analysis (plasma Aβ42, Aβ40, p-tau217, NfL, GFAP; CSF Aβ42, Aβ40, total tau), anti-viral antibody titres (VZV, CMV, EBV, HSV-1, HSV-2 IgG/IgM with defined thresholds: VZV IgG >100 mIU/ml, CMV IgG >=6 AE/ml, HSV-1 IgG >1 S/CO, HSV-2 IgG >1 S/CO), and APOE genotyping were performed to characterize the study cohorts. No dose-response comparisons for treatment were reported.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: CD4+ T helper cells (autoreactive, targeting amyloid-β peptide and related TH2-like clusters)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: T-cell reactivity, functional profile (cytokine secretion, co-stimulatory marker expression, gene expression profile)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: emerges/higher reactivity (in preclinical AD), lower/diminished (in MCI)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Subjects at preclinical AD stage can mount a response, displaying a type 2 T-helper profile and reactivity against carboxyl-terminal and mid-sequence peptides derived from linear Aβ 1-42 (not N-terminus). Increased frequency of OX40 and 4-1BB expression (Fig. 5B and C and Supplementary Fig. 7C) observed in cognitively healthy individuals. Increased frequency of CD4+ EM T-cell clusters expressing Fas-receptor (CD95), Programmed Cell Death Receptor 1 (PD-1), Interleukin-4 (IL-4), Interleukin-13 (IL-13) in HCS+ compared to HCS- and MCI+ (Fig. 4F–H). In MCI subjects, antigen-specific immune response was no longer evident; generally decreased reactivity to all peptide pools tested, displaying only weak reactivity against Aβ mid-sequence peptide pool. Diminished antigen reactivity in MCI+ extended even to positive control antigens (Supplementary Fig. 7E–H). Lower frequencies of T helper cell subsets producing IL-4 and IL-13 in Aβ-positive MCI (no specific numerical quantification).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Mediates adaptive immune response against specific antigens; coordinates immune responses; B cell stimulation and antibody production; involved in immune homeostasis and immune checkpoint regulation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Asymptomatic, preclinical Alzheimer's disease stage (HCS+) vs. Mild cognitive impairment (MCI+) due to Alzheimer's disease. Functional analyses in vitro against Aβ antigens.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests a potentially beneficial role in preclinical AD for Aβ clearance via B cell stimulation, but with specificity aimed at less accessible parts of Aβ. Intact reactivity in cognitively healthy individuals indicates a protective mechanism. Decreased immunoreactivity in MCI suggests hypo-responsiveness or exhaustion due to chronic antigen exposure, leading to reduced stimulation of antibody-producing B cells and potentially less immunoglobulins for Aβ plaque clearance. A more TH2 response-related immune profile in preclinical AD could favor a protective adaptive immune response against pathological compounds.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: CD8+ T effector memory cells re-expressing CD45RA (TEMRA cells) / CD57low CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells (frequency)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMCs) / Peripheral blood
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Cell frequency / enrichment / relative abundance (mass cytometry, single-cell transcriptomics)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Early enrichment observed in CSF of preclinical AD subjects. Relative abundance increased in HCS+ compared to HCS- in both CSF and paired blood-derived PBMCs (Fig. 2D and E). Increased relative abundance of CD57low CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells in MCI+ (P = 0.0027) compared to HCS- in PBMCs (Fig. 2H). This increase in MCI+ (P = 0.0021) was confirmed in PBMCs even after adjustment for CMV IgG titres (Fig. 2I). Increased in MCI p-tau217+ compared to HCS p-tau217- in PBMCs, confirmed after CMV IgG adjustment (Supplementary Fig. 3K and L). Single-cell transcriptomics also confirmed the increase of the CD57low CD8+ TEMRA/effector cell cluster in MCI+ compared to HCS- (Fig. 3I). Substantially increased frequencies in the blood of MCI cases and even in the CSF of preclinical AD cases. Increased numbers (replicated finding).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Adaptive immune response, cytotoxic T-cell function with memory capabilities, effector functions, general involvement in neurodegeneration.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Asymptomatic, preclinical Alzheimer's disease stage (HCS+), Mild cognitive impairment (MCI+) due to Alzheimer's disease, and subjects with elevated p-tau217. Early AD continuum.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an early alteration and expansion of these cells in adaptive immune system in asymptomatic AD stages, independent of latent Herpesviridae infections. Associated with early stages of AD continuum; suggests potential general involvement in neurodegeneration; may contribute to a hyper-inflammatory environment in MCI and AD. Associated with AD pathology or neurodegeneration.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: CD4+ Regulatory T cells (Tregs) gene signature and functional immunosuppression
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Gene expression profile (GSEA), relative abundance, functional immunosuppression

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Less immunosuppressive activity (gene signature); unchanged abundance
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Relative abundance was unchanged across diagnostic groups (Fig. 3E and Supplementary Fig. 3H). GSEA revealed significantly decreased enrichment scores for pro-inflammatory (TNF and IL-6 signalling), immunosuppression-related (TGFβ signalling), and Treg maturation-related (IL-2 and STAT5 signalling) gene modules in HCS+ compared to HCS-. Increased anergy-related gene modules were observed in HCS+ (Fig. 3F and Supplementary Table 1). MCI+ displayed an increased enrichment score for pro-inflammatory (IL-6 signalling) and a decreased enrichment score for the immunosuppression-related gene module (TGFβ signalling) compared to HCS- (Fig. 3F). Overall, a less immunosuppressive gene profile and function observed in preclinical AD and MCI subjects.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Immune regulation; suppression of immune responses to maintain tolerance and prevent autoimmunity.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Asymptomatic, preclinical Alzheimer's disease stage (HCS+) and Mild cognitive impairment (MCI+) due to Alzheimer's disease. Early AD continuum.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates altered immune regulation, possible impairment of Treg function, and peripheral tolerance in preclinical AD (HCS+), and a less immunosuppressive Treg and more pro-inflammatory signature in MCI+. This suggests a shift towards reduced immune tolerance, potentially contributing to neurodegeneration and a hyper-inflammatory environment in MCI and AD. May also suggest a possibility of successfully mounting beneficial adaptive immune responses in preclinical AD.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells gene expression profile (transcriptomic signature)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In preclinical AD (HCS+ vs HCS-), GSEA showed significantly decreased scores for pro-inflammatory gene modules (inflammatory response, TNF and IL-6 signalling). In contrast, in MCI+ (vs HCS-), increased enrichment scores of pro-inflammatory gene modules and simultaneously decreased cytotoxicity-related gene modules were observed (Fig. 3J and Supplementary Table 1). Characterized by a pro-inflammatory gene expression profile in MCI subjects. Less pro-inflammatory transcriptomic signature in preclinical AD. This pattern appeared to reverse in individuals at a more advanced disease stage (Aβ-positive MCI), characterized by increased expression of pro-inflammatory gene modules.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Effector T cells involved in pro-inflammatory and cytotoxic immune responses; regulation of immune response and inflammation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Asymptomatic, preclinical Alzheimer's disease stage (HCS+) and Mild cognitive impairment (MCI+) due to Alzheimer's disease. Early AD continuum.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a less pro-inflammatory gene signature in preclinical AD (HCS+), which shifts to a more pro-inflammatory but less cytotoxic gene signature in MCI+, potentially contributing to the hyper-inflammatory environment and neurodegeneration in MCI and AD. Associated with potentially harmful T-cell activity in symptomatic pathology; suggests it may be important to therapeutically target these responses if proven harmful.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: General antigen responsiveness

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Generally decreased in MCI subjects. Diminished antigen reactivity in MCI+ extended even to positive control antigens (Supplementary Fig. 7E–H). No specific quantification reported.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Ability of immune cells to react and mount a response to specific antigens.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) due to Alzheimer's disease.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates altered or impaired general immune function in MCI, suggesting hypo-responsiveness or exhaustion due to chronic antigen exposure.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: CSF Aβ biomarkers (Aβ 42, Aβ 40, Aβ 42/40 ratio)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Protein level (immunoassay), ratio of protein levels

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower Aβ 42/40 ratio associated with Aβ-positivity
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Aβ 42 and Aβ 40 quantified using Simoa Human Neurology 3-plex A immunoassays. Used to categorize participants as 'brain Aβ-negative (high CSF Aβ 42/40 ratio)' or 'Aβ-positive (low CSF Aβ 42/40 ratio)'. Specific absolute values or changes not reported for individual Aβ levels.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Amyloid-beta peptides are key components of amyloid plaques in Alzheimer's disease. The ratio indicates amyloid plaque pathology.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Analysis in individuals with potential preclinical AD and MCI for diagnostic categorization.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Components of CSF AD biomarkers used for brain Aβ-negativity/positivity categorization, directly indicating brain Aβ status and serving as a marker for potential preclinical Alzheimer's disease.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher Centiloid score indicates Aβ positivity
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Aβ positivity defined as FMM Centiloid >12 (maximum 140 MBq of 18 F-flutemetamol tracer).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Direct quantification of amyloid plaque burden in the brain.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Assessment of cerebral Aβ load using PET imaging in HCS and MCI participants.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Marks the transition from absence of pathology to subtle Aβ pathology, used to group participants by Aβ status.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Plasma Aβ biomarkers (Aβ 42, Aβ 40)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Quantified with a customized Neurology 4-plex A platform. Specific quantitative results are not provided.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Amyloid-beta peptides, key components of amyloid plaques in Alzheimer's disease.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Plasma AD biomarker analysis in study populations 2 and 3.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential blood-based biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease pathology.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: phospho-tau 217 (p-tau217)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated plasma levels observed, used to characterize MCI subjects with increased CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells and for subgrouping participants (p-tau217+). Measured with an in-house assay of University of Gothenburg. Specific quantitative results are not provided.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Phosphorylated tau protein, a specific marker for tau pathology in Alzheimer's disease; strongly correlates with brain Aβ and paired helical filament tau (PHFtau) tangles.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Plasma AD biomarker analysis in study populations 2 and 3; MCI subjects; Alzheimer's Disease pathology.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential blood-based biomarker for Alzheimer's disease tauopathy, indicating neurodegeneration and cognitive decline. Stronger indicator of brain Aβ and PHFtau tangles than p-tau181; associated with increased numbers of CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Quantified with a customized Neurology 4-plex A platform. Specific quantitative results are not provided.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential blood-based biomarker for neuroaxonal damage and neurodegeneration.

analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Plasma AD biomarker analysis in study populations 2 and 3.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Quantified using Simoa Human Neurology 3-plex A immunoassays. Specific quantitative results are not provided.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Anti-viral antibody titres (VZV, CMV, EBV, HSV-1, HSV-2 IgG/IgM)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Unchanged (CMV IgG across diagnostic groups); not reported as change for others.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: VZV IgG (>100 mIU/ml), CMV IgG (>=6 AE/ml), HSV-1 IgG (>1 S/CO), HSV-2 IgG (>1 S/CO) thresholds for positivity. VZV IgM, CMV IgM, EBV VCA IgG, EBV VCA IgM, EBV EBNA IgG, HSV-1 IgM, HSV-2 IgM analyzed qualitatively (positive/negative). 40% of subjects positive for anti-CMV IgG; no significant differences in CMV IgG titres between diagnostic groups observed. CMV IgG titres had significant effects on certain T cell landmark nodes.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicates past exposure or active infection to various herpesviruses (Varicella-Zoster Virus, Cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr Virus, Herpes simplex virus types 1 and 2), reflecting humoral immune status.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Serology analysis in preclinical AD and MCI cohorts, used as covariates and for statistical adjustment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates viral immune status, serving as covariates for immune cell analyses. Observed increases in CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells in AD stages remained significant after adjustment for CMV IgG, indicating AD-related immune changes are independent of CMV reactivation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Subjects with 'increased serum levels of C-reactive protein (CRP)' were excluded. Specific quantitative values for 'increased' are not provided.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: High levels indicate systemic inflammation, which could confound study results related to AD biomarkers.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Frequency was reduced in MCI+ compared to HCS- and HCS+ (Supplementary Fig. 6B).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Characterized by activation, inhibitory immune checkpoint marker (CTLA-4), and anti-inflammatory cytokines, suggesting a regulatory or anti-inflammatory profile.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI+) in the Alzheimer's Disease (AD) continuum.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A reduction in this cluster in MCI+ may indicate a shift away from a potentially regulatory or anti-inflammatory profile, contributing to overall immune dysregulation in MCI.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: CD4+ central memory (CM), CD4+ effector memory (EM), regulatory T cells (Tregs), and unconventional T-cell subsets (overall frequencies)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Frequencies were unchanged across the diagnostic groups after applying adjustment for anti-CMV IgG titres (Supplementary Fig. 3F–J).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Various subsets of T lymphocytes with distinct roles in adaptive immunity, memory, and regulation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Early Alzheimer's Disease (AD) continuum, after controlling for CMV infection influence.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Their overall frequencies are not significantly altered across diagnostic groups of early AD stages when adjusted for CMV infection, suggesting that AD-specific immune changes might involve functional rather than solely quantitative shifts in these general subsets.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: B and NK cell landmark nodes

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Only the proportions of B and NK cell landmark nodes were affected by sex (Supplementary Fig. 3M), with age having minor influences (estimates close to 0).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: B cells: antibody production and humoral immunity. NK cells: innate immunity, direct killing of infected or cancerous cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Analysis of demographic factors (age, sex) influencing immune cell proportions in the study cohorts.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Sex is identified as a factor influencing the proportions of these immune cell types, which needs to be considered when analyzing immune profiles. Age had minor influence.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: phospho-tau 181 (p-tau181)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: High plasma levels (no specific numerical quantification provided; used to characterize groups with increased CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells)

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Biomarker for neurofibrillary tangles; associated with neurodegeneration and cognitive decline.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Alzheimer's Disease pathology; individuals with high plasma levels of p-tau181.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates neurodegeneration and cognitive decline; associated with increased numbers of CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells.
